newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: All change! Vienna trams go solo.
newsitem.headline: All change! Vienna trams go solo.

text.p: Conductors on Vienna trams, the world's longest-running, reached the end of the line on Friday when they punched tickets for the last time in the service's 130-year history.
Conductors have watched the Austrian capital's rickety trams trundle from horsepower to steam and finally electricity. Now the last trams with a conductor's perch are bound for Sarajevo in Bosnia.
In the heyday of the 1950s, as many as 3,500 conductors and 1,000 conductresses were employed on Vienna's trams.
The former capital of the Austro-Hungarian empire got its first tram -- albeit horse-drawn -- in 1865. The horsepower was replaced with steam in 1883, and the electric tram followed 14 years later.
